scores.evidence: Verified in code, not summaries. Conflicts: synthesis gate rejects any non-'open' conflict (pipeline/stages.py check_synthesis ~L410-417); agency.apply_candidate refuses dropped/edited/pre-resolved conflicts and untriaged question removal (_conflict_changes, _question_removal_allowed, pipeline/agency.py ~L73-110); conflicts change only via agency.resolve, which archives and resets signoff to draft. Sign-off: agency.approve requires a blocker-free audit, attester != signer (require_distinct, casefold/whitespace-normalised), intact audit log, and binds fingerprint + language_review hash; revisions.require_current_approval re-checks withdrawal, inputs, evidence and fingerprint. Creative: delivery.register content-addresses the exact files (creative_versions/<sha>), approve requires all 7 checks, spec-catalog validation and SoD (approver != registrant, != brief signer), binds draft/approval/language hashes; release re-checks SoD from the records (_recheck_separation), refuses a broken log, writes to a new directory outside the run via staging+rename, records released_by. Withdrawal (release_control.withdraw) persists before archiving and verify --run flags withdrawn packages. Hash-chained audit_log.jsonl with verify_audit_log detecting edit/insert/reorder/truncation and unvouched approval/creative_approval/amendment/withdrawal/release records (pipeline/revisions.py L279-399). Tests: tests/test_governance_controls.py (19 cases) pass; full suite 948 passed, 7 skipped, 48 xfailed. docs/SECURITY.md §3.6 and §4 state the limits honestly (unauthenticated names, coding agents can run decision commands).
defects: The audit-log cross-check vouches only approval.json, creative_approval.json and the amendments/withdrawals/releases lists (revisions._VOUCHED_RECORDS/_VOUCHED_LISTS). A conflict marked status 'resolved_by_human' with any resolved_by name in brief.json, a hand-written language_review.json, clarifications.json decision or coverage_decisions.json entry (brief_binding is a public deterministic digest) is never checked against a matching conflict_resolved / language_attested / question_triaged / coverage_excluded entry; agency.audit only checks that resolution and resolved_by are non-empty strings. A forged 'human' resolution therefore passes audit and approval.

brief.json and the other earlier-stage artifacts are not protected during later model steps (runner.PROTECTED_RUN_PATHS omits brief.json, extracts/, classification.json, fidelity/, verification/); the render and creative agents can rewrite the canonical brief after the synthesis gate passed, e.g. flip conflicts to resolved_by_human — exactly what tests/injection_project/rfp.md asks for — and the render gate checks the in-memory brief, not the file. No test covers a post-synthesis stage tampering with brief.json.

The committed rehearsal evidence is not independently re-verifiable: `python3 -m pipeline.release_control verify-log runs/rehearsal-lifecycle/records` returns valid:false (releases.json[0] and approval_withdrawals.json[0] unvouched) because regenerate.py substitutes $PACKAGE into hashed records, while TRANSCRIPT.md step 35 shows valid:true and GO_LIVE_DECISIONS T-05 cites it as done.

AI coding agents operate this repo and nothing technical stops one from running agency approve/resolve/attest or delivery approve/release with any typed name (SECURITY.md §4.6 open item; no .claude/settings.json deny rules or hook exist).

The --solo-rehearsal SoD waiver trusts the project folder's current data_declaration.json, which is not hashed into input_snapshot.json; flipping an approved project's declaration to 'synthetic' after the run unlocks the waiver at approval and release time.
scores.to_reach_9: Vouch every human decision in the log (each resolved conflict matched to a conflict_resolved entry by index, actor and resolution digest; exclusions, triage decisions and language attestations likewise) and have agency.audit enforce it; freeze earlier-stage artifacts (brief.json, extracts/, classification.json, fidelity/, verification/) during later model steps with deny rules and the integrity check plus tests; bind data_declaration.json into input_snapshot; ship deny rules/hook that keep coding agents off the human-decision commands; make the committed rehearsal records pass verify-log with a test.

scores.evidence: pipeline/agents.py build_command: inline agent definition from a neutral empty cwd (no CLAUDE.md), --tools Read,Write, --permission-prompts none, --setting-sources project,local, --strict-mcp-config, path-scoped allow rules only, deny Write/Edit on read-only dirs and protected records, deny Read/Write/Edit on //**/answer_key.json, deny Bash/WebFetch/WebSearch/NotebookEdit, both given and resolved path spellings (_rule_paths). I confirmed every flag exists in the installed CLI 2.1.280 `claude --help`. Runner stages byte-identical 0444 copies into <run>/inputs and never grants the project folder (runner.stage_inputs, _access_dirs); post-step hash integrity check over skeleton dirs, protected records and originals, also on halt (runner.integrity_state/integrity_violations, ~L259-280, L770-785). unsafe_source_ids refuses traversal ids before any path is built. Verifier findings screened to verbatim source spans and adjudicated (extraction.screen_findings). Rule U in every runtime prompt, enforced by tests/test_prompt_hygiene.py; work orders carry paths, never source text (tests/test_agent_security.py::test_injected_text_never_reaches_a_work_order). Delivery refuses symlinked/SVG assets and validates package filenames and hashes (delivery.current_draft, release_control.verify). docs/SECURITY.md has an asset/threat/control/proof/residual structure that matches the code.
defects: Stage outputs are not frozen once gated: during render and creative steps the agent may still write brief.json, extracts/, classification.json, fidelity/ and verification/ (not in PROTECTED_RUN_PATHS, not in the integrity watched set). An injected instruction that survives into brief content can alter the canonical brief after its gate; tests only simulate a tampering classify step against approval/staged input/config/schema.

Enforcement of the permission rules by the CLI is still unproven: no live canary run exists (SECURITY.md §4.1), no CLI version is recorded or checked at runtime, and stronger substrate flags available in the same CLI are unused: --restricted (confines file tools to the working directories, refuses bypassPermissions) would close residual risk 1 (reads outside granted dirs), and --no-session-persistence would stop full client-content transcripts being stored in the operator profile.
Coding agents can execute the human-decision commands; the repo ships no .claude/settings.json deny rules or PreToolUse hook for them (SECURITY.md §4.6 left open).
Supply chain partly open: requirements.lock has no hashes and CI actions are pinned by tag rather than commit SHA (.github/workflows/quality.yml comments admit it).
scores.to_reach_9: Add per-stage protection of all previously gated artifacts (deny rules + integrity watch) with tests for a tampering render/creative step; add --restricted and --no-session-persistence to build_command and record `claude --version` in the manifest with a minimum-version refusal; run one owner-authorised live canary on tests/injection_project and commit its manifest; commit deny rules/hook for decision commands; hash the lock and SHA-pin the actions.

scores.evidence: pipeline/data_policy.py: missing/invalid data_declaration.json refuses the run before any source is read (runner exit 6), 'approved' requires approval_ref/approved_by/approved_on (no future dates), and approved projects, client config and output are refused inside the repository (check_locations). Sensitivity tier S2/S3 refused at client-config load before any model step (extraction.load_client_config -> gates.enforce_sensitivity_tier), again on classify output, synthesis and every agency read. Answer key excluded from staging and evidence. Release minimisation whitelists deliverable fields (delivery.release public_rows). pipeline/retention.py inventories every byte copy (evidence/, history/, staged inputs/, packages) and session IDs, purges by source SHA or run with attributed tombstones, never silently deletes the audit log, and protects committed evidence. docs/pilot/DATA_PROTECTION.md is a genuine DPIA input pack: personal-data inventory by subject, per-stage flow map of what reaches the provider, WP248 screening, lawful-basis options, per-artifact retention schedule, rights procedure, Art. 28 processor checklist, effort-data purpose limitation, special-category screening step; legal judgements are correctly marked OWNER/DPO TO CONFIRM. Pseudonymised scorecard (L1/L2).
defects: Session persistence is left as 'OPERATOR TO CONFIRM' (DATA_PROTECTION.md §6, §8, §11) although the documented CLI 2.1.280 offers --no-session-persistence for --print; build_command does not pass it, so every model run stores full source content and outputs in the operator's CLI profile, outside every retention control.

The fixtures-only boundary rests on a self-asserted {"data_class": "synthetic"} with no automated personal-data or special-category pre-screen (acknowledged open, §1/§11); the same self-assertion also unlocks the SoD solo-rehearsal waiver, and the declaration is not hashed into input_snapshot.json, so it can change after a run without invalidating it.

No data-minimisation option is analysed for the model flow: classify receives the full text of every source (§3 flow map) although it needs little more than headers and the client config; speaker pseudonymisation is listed as open without an evaluation plan.

The committed graded run runs/tier3 still carries the case-study author's real name as signer/resolver (acknowledged; historical, read-only), so the repository itself is not strictly synthetic-only in its personal data.
scores.to_reach_9: Pass --no-session-persistence (verified against the pinned CLI) and update the retention schedule accordingly; add a deterministic, warning-level personal-data/special-category pre-screen (emails, phone numbers, Greek+English term list in config/) whose result is recorded in the manifest and required as 'screened_by/screened_on' before an approved run; hash data_declaration.json into input_snapshot; document a minimisation analysis for classify and a pseudonymisation evaluation plan.

moves.title: Freeze every gated artifact during later model steps
moves.rationale: The biggest real bypass: after synthesis passes, the render and creative agents can still write brief.json (and extracts/, classification.json, fidelity/, verification/), e.g. forge a 'resolved_by_human' conflict, and neither permission rules nor the integrity check notice. Closing it turns the existing integrity mechanism into a complete one.
moves.concrete_changes: pipeline/runner.py: make _access_dirs(ctx, step) stage-aware — protected = PROTECTED_RUN_PATHS + outputs of all earlier steps (classification.json after step 2; fidelity/ after 3; extracts/, verification/ after 4; conflict_candidates.json after 5; brief.json after 6; brief_el.md/brief_en.md after 7); integrity_state uses the same set. pipeline/agents.py unchanged (it already turns protected paths into deny rules). tests/test_agent_security.py: parametrised 'obedient render/creative handler' cases that rewrite brief.json (conflict -> resolved_by_human), an extract and classification.json, each asserting stage_failed with 'integrity:'. docs/SECURITY.md §3.2/§3.4: list the per-stage protected set.

moves.title: Vouch every human decision in the audit log and enforce it in audit
moves.rationale: verify_audit_log only vouches approvals and three lists; forged conflict resolutions, exclusions, triage decisions and language attestations pass. Tamper-evidence should cover every decision the approval relies on.
moves.concrete_changes: pipeline/agency.py resolve: log details {conflict, resolved_by, resolution_sha256}; exclude/answer: log entry_sha256 of the stored decision; attest: log the record hash, and approve logs a 'language_attestation_transferred' entry with the new hash. pipeline/revisions.py verify_audit_log: for each conflict with status resolved_by_human in brief.json require a matching conflict_resolved entry (index, actor == resolved_by, resolution digest); each coverage_decisions/clarifications entry and the current language_review.json must be vouched. agency.audit adds verify_audit_log problems as blockers. data_declaration.json hashed into input_snapshot at runner start and intake so a flipped declaration invalidates approval and any solo waiver. tests/test_governance_controls.py: hand-written resolution, exclusion with computed binding, attestation and declaration flip each blocked.

moves.title: Harden the runtime substrate flags: session persistence off, restricted mode, CLI version recorded
moves.rationale: The same CLI (2.1.280) offers --no-session-persistence and --restricted; using them removes an uncontrolled copy of all client content from the operator profile and confines file tools to granted directories (SECURITY residual risk 1), and a recorded version makes permission semantics auditable.
moves.concrete_changes: pipeline/agents.py build_command: add '--no-session-persistence' and '--restricted' (keep --tools/--strict-mcp-config); invoke(): capture `claude --version` once per process and refuse below a MIN_CLI_VERSION constant; runner writes cli_version into run_manifest.json. tests/test_agent_security.py::test_command_isolates_the_substrate_and_scopes_every_tool asserts both flags. tools/replay/claude accepts them. docs/SECURITY.md §3.2/§4.1 and docs/pilot/DATA_PROTECTION.md §6/§8/§11 replace 'OPERATOR TO CONFIRM' for session files with the control; retention.session_ids documented as legacy-only.

moves.title: Keep coding agents off the human-decision commands
moves.rationale: The repo is operated by Claude Code and Codex; SECURITY.md §4.6 admits nothing stops an agent from running approve/resolve/release under a typed name. A committed deny layer makes the 'no model runs them' policy technical.
moves.concrete_changes: Add .claude/settings.json with permissions.deny for Bash patterns covering `python3 -m pipeline.agency (approve|resolve|attest|exclude|answer|apply|carry-decisions)`, `pipeline.delivery (register|approve|release)`, `pipeline.release_control withdraw`, `pipeline.retention purge` (and `python3 pipeline/...` spellings), plus a PreToolUse hook script scripts/deny_decision_commands.sh as belt and braces; equivalent rule text in AGENTS.md / .codex config; tests/test_prompt_hygiene.py (or a new test) asserts the deny list covers every decision subcommand parsed from the argparse definitions. Update SECURITY.md §4.6 from open to controlled.

moves.title: Make the committed rehearsal records pass verify-log
moves.rationale: The rehearsal is the only committed end-to-end proof of release, withdrawal and tamper-evidence, yet verify-log on runs/rehearsal-lifecycle/records returns valid:false because regenerate.py rewrites hashed paths to $PACKAGE; a reviewer who re-checks finds a contradiction with TRANSCRIPT.md step 35.
moves.concrete_changes: runs/rehearsal-lifecycle/regenerate.py: release to a path that needs no substitution (e.g. a relative sibling 'package' directory under the rehearsal root) or stop substituting inside records that are hashed into the log; regenerate. Add tests/test_rehearsal_records.py asserting release_control.verify_log(records)['valid'] and verify(records/package, run=records) behave as the transcript states (withdrawn: true). Note in docs/pilot/GO_LIVE_DECISIONS.md T-05 that the committed records re-verify.

moves.title: Deterministic personal-data pre-screen and declaration hardening
moves.rationale: The fixtures-only boundary and the DPIA pack rely on a self-asserted declaration and a manual special-category screen; a warning-level deterministic screen with a recorded outcome gives the DPO evidence before the first approved run.
moves.concrete_changes: New pipeline/data_screen.py (no model calls): regex for e-mail addresses, phone numbers, IBAN-like strings, plus a Greek+English special-category term list in config/special_category_terms.json; run by intake and runner for every project, results in run_manifest.json 'data_screen'; for data_class 'approved', data_policy requires 'screened_by' and 'screened_on' fields and refuses if the screen has unacknowledged hits. Tests with a synthetic hit fixture. DATA_PROTECTION.md §1/§10/§11 updated; add a minimisation note for classify (headers-only option to evaluate).

moves.title: One owner-authorised live injection canary
moves.rationale: Argv is tested byte for byte, but whether the CLI actually refuses protected writes and answer-key reads is unproven (SECURITY.md §4.1). One live run on the existing synthetic injection project converts the main residual risk into evidence.
moves.concrete_changes: Add eval/injection_canary.py: runs pipeline/runner.py on tests/injection_project to a scratch out dir, then asserts integrity pass, no approval.json/schema/config change, no /tmp/leak.json, extraction_note 'embedded instruction not followed' present, manifest cli_version recorded; commit the manifest and verdict under runs/injection-canary-01/ with a .gitignore exception; cite in SECURITY.md §3.1/§4.1.

moves.title: Close the supply-chain items
moves.rationale: Unhashed lock and tag-pinned actions are the remaining generic supply-chain gaps a reviewer will flag.
moves.concrete_changes: Regenerate requirements.lock with `pip-compile --generate-hashes` and install with --require-hashes in scripts/check.sh and CI; replace actions/checkout@v4 and actions/setup-python@v5 with full commit SHAs (tag as comment); pin ruff via the lock; add Dependabot/renovate config only if allowed (no integration: otherwise document a manual monthly refresh in docs/SECURITY.md §3.7).

overall: The trust layer is well above typical MVP standard: least-privilege subagent invocation with flags verified against the installed CLI, staged read-only inputs, a post-step integrity check, verbatim-screened verifier findings, human-only conflict resolution, separation of duties, content-addressed creative approval bound by hashes, attributed release and withdrawal, a hash-chained audit log, and a data-declaration gate backed by a serious DPIA input pack and retention tooling. SECURITY.md is honest about its limits. What keeps each aspect at 7 is a small set of concrete gaps, not missing design: artifacts that already passed their gate (above all brief.json) stay writable by later model steps; the audit log does not vouch conflict resolutions, exclusions, triage or attestations, so a forged 'human' resolution passes; the committed rehearsal records fail verify-log; coding agents can run the decision commands; and available CLI hardening (--no-session-persistence, --restricted) is unused while session storage is still marked 'to confirm'. Moves 1-3 and 5 are small, need no owner decision, and would move human_governance and security_injection to 8+; data_protection needs move 3 plus the pre-screen (move 6).
